risks.title: Cyberattacks disrupting operations
risks.score_rationale: Risk is cited at the top of risk factors with a dedicated committee at board level, strong language ('cybersecurity threats'), and reinforced governance, indicating critical exposure. Dependence on IT systems for real-time production amplifies potential impact.

risks.title: Declining photomask demand
risks.score_rationale: The document repeatedly mentions that technology evolution (circuit design, alternative methods) could reduce or eliminate the need for photomasks. Language is concerning ('could reduce or eliminate'), with existential impact on the business model.

risks.title: Dependence on advanced technology nodes
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes substantial investment in sub-28nm and EUV nodes. Delay or failure in these technologies would have major impact, as indicated by rising capex ($330 million) and competitive pressure.

risks.title: Underutilized production capacity
risks.score_rationale: Risk is explicitly mentioned with the term 'excess or underutilized production capacity' and linked to revenue decline. The capital-intensive nature of the model increases severity.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks affecting sites
risks.score_rationale: Company operates in China, South Korea, Taiwan, Germany, with owned or leased facilities. Mention of 'geopolitical impacts' on revenues corroborates this risk. Geographic concentration increases vulnerability.

risks.title: Undisclosed legal litigation
risks.score_rationale: Risk is referenced to Note 16 without detail, suggesting possible but unquantified exposure. Inclusion in 10-K indicates vigilance, but without marked verbal intensity.

risks.title: Exposure to semiconductor industry volatility
risks.score_rationale: Sector is described as 'volatile' with overcapacity cycles and price erosion. This risk is recurring, cited as directly affecting revenues and profitability, with strong language ('diminished product demand', 'erosion of selling prices').

ai_positioning.summary: Photronics benefits indirectly from AI growth through increased demand for photomasks for data centers and AI applications, although AI is not mentioned as a direct focus area.
evidence: Data centers that support AI implementation mentioned as key end market
